headline: Alignment-free k-mers separate viral sequence classes; pangenome graphs benchmarked
label: Alignment Free Pathogen Genomics
summary: Alignment-free k-mer features now distinguish closely related pathogen sequences and expose representation effects in pangenome graph construction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is alignment-free sequence representation, applied either to supervised classification or to comparative benchmarking. A random forest on alignment-free k-mer features separates pre- and post-Omicron Delta spike sequences at 93% accuracy and identifies persistent mutations. PORT-EK-v2, an updated k-mer pipeline, finds over-represented HIV-1 sequence regions that distinguish DNA from RNA across group M subtypes. The pangenome-graph study is a different kind of work: it benchmarks six tools on E. coli O157:H7 genomes rather than predicting a phenotype, and reports that representation strategy and assembly completeness drive graph size, topology, and runtime. What is new across these items is the use of k-mer-level, alignment-free features for viral nucleic-acid and variant-period discrimination, alongside systematic evaluation of how graph representation choices shape bacterial pangenome analysis.
